result.noRegion.diia:
Plates of the DІ series are issued when a vehicle is re-registered online through Diia, instead of at a service centre (TSC).
What is Diia - Ukraine's state app and portal for e-services (documents, registers, vehicle services).
What registering via Diia means - the new owner re-registers the vehicle remotely, with the sale contract concluded through e-services, and gets a plate of the DІ series.
Why there is no region - the letters show how the service was ordered, not where the car is registered, so the plate says nothing about the owner's oblast.
result.noRegion.driverCabinet:
Plates of the ЕD series are issued when a vehicle is re-registered through the Driver's Cabinet (the MIA's online service) instead of at a service centre (TSC).
What is the Driver's Cabinet - the Ministry of Internal Affairs' online account for drivers and vehicle owners.
Why there is no region - the letters show how the service was ordered, not where the car is registered, so the plate says nothing about the owner's oblast.
result.noRegion.generic:
The first letters of this plate are not a regional code, so we cannot tell the region. Typical reasons:
Online-service series - DІ (Diia) and ЕD (Driver's Cabinet) plates carry the service channel, not a region.
Temporary, transit or customs plates - issued for a limited period and not tied to an oblast.
Foreign or non-standard plates - a different country's or an unusual format.
Registry data noise - a typo or an unusual entry in the source open data.

auctions.fact.1: US insurers sell cars written off after an accident ("salvage") at auctions like Copart and IAAI - often at a fraction of the market price, which is why they are so popular with Ukrainian buyers.
auctions.fact.2: After repair such a car can look perfect, but hidden damage, replaced airbags or a straightened frame are the usual risks - an auction photo shows the real condition before the repair.
auctions.fact.3: Auction archives are one of the few places where an odometer reading from the time of sale can be compared with what the seller says now.
auctions.fact.4: Cars from Korea and Europe mostly appear on dealer marketplaces rather than public salvage archives, so a missing hit there says little.

ownerType.private.desc: Registered to an individual. Mostly passenger cars (~83%), nearly all motorcycles and mopeds; the average vehicle is about 18 years old.
ownerType.legal.desc: A company, organisation or state body: fleets, leasing, dealers, taxis, services. One in three is a truck (vs 1 in 13 for private owners); the average vehicle is about 15 years old.
ownerType.why: Why only two? The open registry publishes just a person / legal-entity flag. Names, IDs and addresses are withheld to protect personal data, so finer types (sole proprietor, leasing, state) cannot be told apart.
field.about.body:
Body type exactly as written in the registry (Ukrainian names). A suffix like “-B” is the driving-licence category the vehicle falls under (A motorcycle, B car, C truck, D bus, E with trailer).
СЕДАН (sedan) - separate boot, usually 4 doors
ХЕТЧБЕК (hatchback) - boot shares the cabin, rear tailgate
УНІВЕРСАЛ / КОМБІ (wagon) - long roof, large load space
КУПЕ (coupe) - two doors, sporty roofline
ПІКАП (pickup) - open cargo bed behind the cab
ПАСАЖИРСЬКИЙ (passenger) - minivan or passenger van for 5+ seats
ВАНТАЖОПАСАЖИРСЬКИЙ (cargo-passenger) - van with seats and a cargo area
ФУРГОН (van) - closed cargo box; МАЛОТОНАЖНИЙ = light-duty; РЕФРИЖЕРАТОР = refrigerated
БОРТОВИЙ / ТЕНТОВАНИЙ - flatbed truck, open or with a tarpaulin cover
САМОСКИД (dump truck) - tipping cargo bed
СІДЛОВИЙ ТЯГАЧ (tractor unit) - pulls a semi-trailer
АВТОБУС / МІКРОАВТОБУС (bus / minibus) - carries passengers
МОТОЦИКЛ / МОПЕД (motorcycle / moped) - two-wheelers
ПР- (trailer) - towed behind a vehicle, e.g. ПР-БОРТОВИЙ flatbed trailer, ПР-ЛЕГКОВИЙ car trailer
Н/ПР- (semi-trailer) - rests partly on the tractor unit, e.g. Н/ПР-КОНТЕЙНЕРОВОЗ container carrier
ПЛАТФОРМА (platform) - flat load deck without sides
field.about.capacity:
Engine displacement - the total volume of all cylinders, in cubic centimetres (cc). Roughly: more cc, more power and more fuel.
Up to 1000 cc - city cars
1000–1600 cc - everyday family cars
1600–2500 cc - larger cars and SUVs
2500 cc and up - powerful or heavy vehicles. In Ukraine the import customs duty and the luxury tax depend on it.
field.about.power:
Peak engine power in kilowatts (kW). 1 kW ≈ 1.34 hp. Shown for vehicles registered since 2026; for an electric car it replaces the engine capacity.
50 kW - ≈ 67 hp
100 kW - ≈ 134 hp
150 kW - ≈ 201 hp
field.about.color: The body colour recorded at registration. It is what the owner or dealer declared and can differ from the real colour after a repaint - a repaint should be re-registered, but often isn’t.
field.about.fuel:
The fuel the engine runs on, as registered.
Gasoline (petrol) and diesel - the most common
Gas / LPG - a petrol car converted to run on gas (often bi-fuel)
Electric - battery only, no engine capacity
Hybrid - combustion engine plus an electric motor
field.about.weight:
Two figures in kilograms (kg), separated by a slash.
Kerb weight - the empty vehicle with fluids, without driver, passengers or cargo
Gross weight - the maximum permitted weight when fully loaded. The difference is the payload.
field.about.kind: The vehicle class from the registration papers: passenger car, truck, bus, motorcycle, trailer, etc. Together with the body type it tells what the vehicle is meant to do.
field.about.purpose: What the vehicle is registered for. The registry uses three values:
field.about.ownersCount: Estimated number of owners: the first registration plus every re-registration due to a change of owner. The registry holds no identity data, so this is an estimate: a sale without re-registration is invisible, and history only starts in 2013. VINs appear in the registry only since 2021, so older plates and owners of the same car are not linked by VIN.
field.about.owner: Whether the current owner is a private person or a legal entity (company). The registry never shows names or any personal data.
field.about.regDate: The date of the latest registration operation in the registry - the first registration, a re-registration after a sale, or a change of data. It is not necessarily the date the car was built or first sold. The full chain is in the history below.
field.about.dep: The MVS service centre (ТСЦ МВС) that carried out the latest registration. Tap it to see it on the map.
field.about.koatuu:
KOATUU - the old Ukrainian classifier of administrative-territorial units. A 10-digit code of the settlement where the owner is registered (it names the place, not the street address).
Digits 1–2 - oblast (48 Mykolaiv, 63 Kharkiv, 80 Kyiv city…); the app shows its name next to the code
Digits 3–5 - district or city of oblast significance
Digits 6–8 - settlement or village council
Digits 9–10 - the settlement itself
Example: 4823355100 → Mykolaiv Oblast (48), then district, council and settlement
field.about.vin: Vehicle Identification Number - a unique 17-character code of the car, like its passport number. It stays with the car for life, unlike the plate. Open it to decode the maker, year, engine and more. VINs appear in the registry only since 2021, so older plates and owners of the same car are not linked by VIN.
section.about.vin:
Everything the 17-character VIN reveals about the car, decoded by the free US NHTSA database and our registry.
Parts of the VIN - manufacturer, model descriptor, check digit, model year, plant, serial number
Specs - body, drive, engine, transmission, safety equipment
Less data for cars made for the European market - NHTSA covers US-market vehicles best
VIN data only exists since 2021 - older records of the same car are not linked by VIN.
section.about.history:
Every registration operation on record for this plate and for this VIN, newest first.
First registration, re-registration after a sale, change of colour, engine or documents
Plate history - everyone who ever wore this plate, including reassignments
VIN history - every plate this one vehicle has had
Only operations from 2013 onward are in the open data
VIN data only exists since 2021 - older records of the same car are not linked by VIN.
section.about.emissions:
Estimated fuel use and CO₂ for this make, model, year and engine - reference data, not a measurement of this particular car.
EPA - the US fuel-economy database
EEA - official EU type-approval CO₂ data (2010+)
The lower the g/km of CO₂ and the litres per 100 km, the cheaper and cleaner the car is to run
section.about.photos:
Stock photos of this make and model from Pixabay, to give a rough idea of the look.
Illustrative only - not this specific car, so colour, trim and condition will differ
May show other generations or be empty for rare models
section.about.wiki:
A short summary of the make and model from Wikipedia, with a photo and a link to the full article.
It describes the model in general - generation, history, specs - not this specific car
The language follows the app language when an article exists, otherwise English
section.about.nearby:
A Google Maps search around your current location for services this car may need.
Mechanics - repair shops and service stations
Brand dealers - official dealers of this make
Insurance - insurance agents
The browser asks for your location when you open the section; it is only used for the map and is not stored

vin.since2021.body: The open registry started publishing VINs only in 2021. Older records have no VIN, so a car's earlier plates and owners are not linked by VIN and may be missing here.
vin.since2021.noVin: No VIN is published for this plate: VINs appear in the open registry only since 2021. The same car may be listed under another plate with a VIN - search by VIN to find all of them.

plate.seg.region.desc: The first characters show which region issued the plate. Here: {{region}}. It is where the plate was issued, not necessarily where the car is now - an owner can keep a plate and put it on another car.

vin.seg.wmi.desc: World Manufacturer Identifier (WMI), 3 characters: the 1st marks the country or region, the 2nd the manufacturer, the 3rd the vehicle type or division. Here: {{manufacturer}}, built in {{country}}.
vin.seg.vds.title: VDS - vehicle descriptor
vin.seg.vds.desc: Vehicle Descriptor Section (VDS), positions 4–8: model, body, engine and restraint codes. The manufacturer defines them, so only NHTSA (US-market cars) or the maker's own catalog can decode them. Decoded descriptor: {{descriptor}}.
vin.seg.vds.descRaw: Vehicle Descriptor Section (VDS), positions 4–8: model, body, engine and restraint codes. The manufacturer defines them, so only NHTSA (US-market cars) or the maker's own catalog can decode them. NHTSA has no decode for this VIN; the raw code is {{descriptor}}.
vin.seg.check.title: Check digit
vin.seg.check.desc: Computed from all other characters; it catches typos and fake VINs. 9th position.

vin.seg.year.desc: This letter or digit encodes the model year. Here: {{year}}.
vin.seg.plant.title: Assembly plant
vin.seg.plant.desc: Code of the factory that built the car. Here: {{city}}, {{country}}.
vin.seg.serial.title: Serial number
vin.seg.serial.desc: Production sequence number - unique to this car within its plant and year.

origin.explainer.title: What is this and why does it matter?
origin.explainer.what: A timeline of where this car's brand comes from, who owns it, where the car was most likely assembled and how it reached Ukraine. A step appears only when we have the data; nothing is guessed.
origin.explainer.sources: Brand country, founding year, headquarters and owners come from Wikidata. The plant comes from the NHTSA VIN decoder or, failing that, from the country of the VIN prefix.
origin.explainer.why: A "German" car can be built in Mexico or China, and the plant often affects quality, recalls and parts availability.
origin.explainer.disclaimer: This is brand and plant level information, not a guarantee about this exact car.
origin.ukraine.imported: Brought in from abroad as a used car
origin.warn.mismatch: The VIN prefix belongs to {{maker}}, while the registry lists {{brand}}. This can be a rebadged model or a data error.
origin.hint.northAmerica: Hint: this VIN was built for North America, so the car may be a US or Canada specification.
origin.hint.differs: Hint: the brand is from {{brand}} but this car was assembled in {{plant}}. Many brands build cars abroad.

vin.typical.why: Not read from this VIN - taken from other vehicles of the same make, model and year (Dutch register, VehiclesDB catalog, EPA / EEA). Your exact car may differ.
vin.typical.inputs: The make / model / year used for the match are estimates too (≈ {{sources}}).
vin.derived.title: Some details are estimated, not decoded
vin.derived.why: The US NHTSA database has no full record for this VIN - common for cars that were never sold in the US or Canada. Values marked ≈ were filled in another way, so treat them as a good hint rather than a full decode:
vin.derived.registry.label: registry
vin.derived.registry.hint: taken from the Ukrainian state registry record for this VIN (what the car was registered as).
vin.derived.wmi.label: VIN prefix
vin.derived.wmi.hint: read from the first 3 VIN characters, which identify the manufacturer and country. It shows who made the car and where, not the model or trim.
vin.derived.yearCode.label: year code
vin.derived.yearCode.hint: read from the 10th VIN character, which encodes the model year. The code repeats every 30 years, so the most recent plausible year is shown.

section.about.assists:
The driver-assist and safety systems the VIN decoder lists for this car.
Standard - fitted on this trim
Optional - offered on this trim, may not be on this exact car
SAE level - how much the car can steer and brake for you, from 0 (nothing) to 5 (everything); a driver-assist rating, not a promise of self-driving
vin.assists.explainer.title: What is this, and why can it be empty?
vin.assists.explainer.what: Systems that help the driver or protect people in a crash: stability control, emergency braking, lane keeping, blind-spot warning, adaptive cruise and more. They come from the VIN decoder (NHTSA).
vin.assists.explainer.why: Useful when buying or checking a listing: it shows what safety kit this trim shipped with, so you can compare it with what the seller claims.
vin.assists.explainer.empty: The list is often empty. The US database fills these fields mainly for cars built for the US market from about 2018; cars made for Europe and older cars usually return nothing. No chips does not mean the car has no systems, and the section is hidden when there is nothing to show.
vin.assists.explainer.caveat: Standard or optional describes the trim, not this exact car: an optional system may be missing. Check the car itself or the maker's documentation.
vin.assist.sae: SAE automation level: {{level}} (of 5). A driver-assist rating, not self-driving.

vin.details.title: All details
vin.info.descriptor: The model-specific part of the VIN (positions 4–9) with the unknown characters replaced by *, plus the year and plant codes.
vin.info.manufacturer: The legal entity that built the vehicle. It can differ from the brand on the badge (e.g. a corporation owning several makes).
vin.info.series: A sub-model or body-style detail that the manufacturer encodes in the VIN.
vin.info.trim: The equipment level of this model, e.g. LX, EX, Limited.
vin.info.vehicleType: Regulatory class: passenger car, multipurpose passenger vehicle (SUV/MPV), truck, bus, trailer, motorcycle…
vin.info.bodyClass: The body shape: sedan, hatchback, wagon, SUV, pickup…
vin.info.doors: Number of doors, counting a hatchback or tailgate as one.
vin.info.driveType: Which wheels the engine drives: FWD (front), RWD (rear), AWD/4WD (all four).
vin.info.transmission:
How engine power reaches the wheels.
Manual (MT) - you shift gears with a clutch pedal; simple, cheap, durable
Automatic (AT) - torque-converter gearbox with 6–10 speeds; smooth and tough (Toyota, BMW’s ZF 8-speed)
CVT - belt and pulleys with no fixed gears; very smooth and economical but can feel “rubbery” (Nissan, Subaru, Toyota, Hyundai)
DCT / DSG (dual-clutch) - two clutches for fast shifts (VW DSG, Ford PowerShift); efficient but can be jerky at low speed
AMT (automated manual) - manual gearbox shifted by a robot; cheap, slow shifts (older Fiat, Opel Easytronic)
Electric cars use a single-speed reduction gear.
vin.info.gvwr:
Gross vehicle weight rating: the maximum safe loaded weight (car + fuel + passengers + cargo) set by the manufacturer. NHTSA groups it into US classes 1–8:
Class 1 - up to 6,000 lb (2,722 kg): cars, small SUVs, minivans (Corolla, Golf, Honda CR-V)
Class 2 - 6,001–10,000 lb (up to 4,536 kg): full-size pickups and vans (Ford F-150, Sprinter)
Class 3 - 10,001–14,000 lb (up to 6,350 kg): heavy-duty pickups, large vans (Ford F-350)
Class 4–6 - up to 26,000 lb (11,793 kg): delivery and box trucks
Class 7–8 - over 26,000 lb: semi-trucks, buses, heavy haulage
vin.info.cylinders:
Number of engine cylinders - the chambers where fuel burns and pushes the pistons. More cylinders usually means smoother and more powerful, but thirstier.
2–3 - tiny city engines (Fiat 500 TwinAir, Ford EcoSport 1.0, Toyota Aygo)
4 - the everyday standard (VW Golf 1.5, Kia Ceed 1.6, Toyota Corolla 1.8)
5 - rarer, distinctive sound (Audi RS3, older Volvo T5)
6 - V6 or in-line six, smooth and strong (BMW M340i, Toyota Camry 3.5)
8 - V8, big power and torque (Ford Mustang GT, Mercedes E63)
12 - luxury and supercars (Ferrari 812, Rolls-Royce Phantom)
vin.info.displacement:
Total volume swept by all pistons - the “engine size”. Bigger usually means more power and torque, and more fuel burnt. 1000 cc = 1 litre ≈ 61 cubic inches.
1.0–1.4 L - small city cars (Hyundai i10, VW Polo)
1.5–2.0 L - typical family cars (Kia Ceed, Toyota Corolla, VW Golf)
2.5–3.5 L - larger sedans and SUVs (Toyota Camry, Ford Explorer)
4.0 L and up - V8 trucks and performance cars (Ford F-150, Mercedes E63)
Turbo engines get more power from less volume: a 1.5 L turbo can match an older 2.0 L.
vin.info.engineModel:
The manufacturer’s engine family name or code. It tells you the generation and design - handy for finding parts, known issues and service intervals. A trailing II / III usually means a later generation.
Gamma / Gamma II - Hyundai-Kia 1.4–1.6 L four-cylinder petrol (Kia Ceed, Rio, Hyundai Elantra, Solaris)
Theta II - Hyundai-Kia 2.0–2.4 L petrol (Sonata, Optima, Sportage)
EcoBoost - Ford turbo petrol family, 1.0 L three-cylinder to 3.5 L V6
TSI / TFSI - VW-Audi turbo petrol (Golf, Octavia, Audi A3)
Dynamic Force - Toyota 2.0–2.5 L petrol (Corolla, Camry, RAV4)
K-series - Honda 2.0–2.4 L petrol (Civic Si, Accord, CR-V)
B48 / N20 - BMW turbo four-cylinders
vin.info.engineConfig:
Cylinder layout of the engine.
In-line (I3, I4, I6) - one row of cylinders; simple and compact, most four-cylinders
V (V6, V8, V12) - two angled banks; short engine, suits many cylinders
Flat / boxer (H4, H6) - horizontally opposed; low centre of gravity (Subaru, Porsche 911)
Rotary, W - rarer designs (Mazda RX-8, VW W12)
vin.info.horsepower:
Peak engine power. 1 hp ≈ 0.746 kW, so 120 hp ≈ 89 kW. US data uses SAE horsepower; European “PS” / “к.с.” (metric hp) is about 1.4% smaller.
Under 100 hp - city cars (Hyundai i10 ≈ 67–87 hp)
100–150 hp - everyday family cars (Kia Ceed 1.6 ≈ 120–130 hp)
150–250 hp - brisk: hot hatches and large SUVs (VW Golf GTI ≈ 245 hp)
250 hp and up - sports cars and big V6/V8 engines (Ford Mustang GT ≈ 450+ hp)
vin.info.kilowatts:
Peak engine power in kilowatts (kW), the SI unit used on European registration papers. 1 kW ≈ 1.34 hp.
50 kW - ≈ 67 hp
75 kW - ≈ 100 hp
100 kW - ≈ 134 hp
150 kW - ≈ 201 hp
vin.info.fuelPrimary: The main fuel: gasoline, diesel, electric, LPG…
vin.info.fuelSecondary: A second fuel the engine can use (e.g. bi-fuel gasoline + LPG).
vin.info.valveTrain:
How the valves that let air in and exhaust out are driven by camshafts.
SOHC (single overhead cam) - one camshaft per bank; simple and compact, common in older and economy engines
DOHC (dual overhead cam) - two camshafts per bank; better airflow and high-rev power, now the norm, usually 4 valves per cylinder
OHV (pushrod) - camshaft in the engine block; compact and torquey, used in many US V8s (Chevrolet small-block)
Variable valve timing (VVT, VTEC, VANOS) is added on top of these to improve efficiency and power.
vin.info.turbo:
A turbocharger uses exhaust gas to force more air into the cylinders, making more power from a smaller engine.
Typical in downsized 1.0–1.5 L petrols (Ford EcoBoost, VW TSI)
Almost every modern diesel is turbocharged
Trade-off: more heat and complexity - wants good oil and a short cool-down after hard driving
vin.info.electrification:
Hybrid or electric system level.
MHEV - mild hybrid: a small 48 V motor assists the engine but cannot drive the car alone (Suzuki Swift Hybrid, many Audi and Mercedes)
HEV - full hybrid: can drive short distances on electricity and charges itself (Toyota Prius, Corolla Hybrid)
PHEV - plug-in hybrid: bigger battery, roughly 40–80 km electric range, charges from the grid (Toyota RAV4 Prime, Volvo T8)
BEV - battery electric: no combustion engine (Tesla Model 3, Nissan Leaf)
FCEV - hydrogen fuel cell (Toyota Mirai)
vin.info.seatBelt: Belt type fitted: manual (you buckle up) or with automatic components.
vin.info.pretensioner: Pyrotechnic device that tightens the belt in the first milliseconds of a crash.
vin.info.tpms: Direct = a pressure sensor inside every wheel. Indirect = estimated from wheel-speed (ABS) data, less precise.
vin.info.airbagFront: Frontal airbags in the steering wheel and dashboard, by seat row.
vin.info.airbagSide: Airbags in the seat or door that protect the torso in a side impact.
vin.info.airbagCurtain: Inflatable curtains along the side windows that protect heads in side impacts and rollovers.
vin.info.airbagKnee: Airbag under the dashboard that protects legs and keeps the occupant in position.
vin.info.abs: Anti-lock braking: stops the wheels locking so you can steer while braking hard.
vin.info.esc: Electronic stability control: brakes individual wheels to stop a skid. Mandatory on new cars in the US and EU.
vin.info.tc: Traction control: limits wheel spin when accelerating on slippery surfaces.
vin.info.fcw: Warns the driver of an imminent frontal collision.
vin.info.dbs: Adds braking force when the driver brakes too lightly to avoid a collision.
vin.info.aeb: Automatic emergency braking that detects pedestrians.
vin.info.acc: Cruise control that keeps a set distance to the vehicle ahead.
vin.info.ldw: Warns when the car drifts out of its lane without signalling.
vin.info.lka: Gently steers the car back into its lane.
vin.info.bsw: Warns of vehicles in the blind spot when changing lanes.
vin.info.rcta: Warns of cross traffic when reversing out of a parking space.
vin.info.keyless: Push-button start with a key fob that stays in your pocket.
vin.info.drl: Lights that switch on automatically in daytime to make the car more visible.

verification.bdr.about:
A Ministry of Internal Affairs service for finding traffic violations that cameras recorded automatically (no stop by police) for a plate.
BDR - bezpeka dorozhnoho rukhu, road traffic safety
PDR - Pravyla dorozhnoho rukhu, the traffic rules
MVS - the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Ukraine
verification.mtsbu.about:
Checks whether a vehicle has a valid compulsory third-party liability policy, which covers damage to other parties in a crash.
OSCPV (OSCPVVTZ) - compulsory civil liability insurance for owners of land vehicles, commonly called "avtotsyvilka"
MTSBU - Motor (Transport) Insurance Bureau of Ukraine: the association of insurers that keeps the central database of OSCPV policies
verification.otk.about:
Shows whether a vehicle has a valid technical inspection protocol. It is mandatory for some vehicle categories (e.g. trucks, buses, taxis); for private cars, no protocol does not necessarily mean a violation.
OTK - obovyazkovyi tekhnichnyi kontrol, mandatory periodic roadworthiness and safety inspection
TZ - transportnyi zasib, a vehicle
The service runs on the open-data portal of the Main Service Centre of the MVS (HSC)
verification.license.about:
Shows whether a driving licence issued in Ukraine is valid. It needs the licence series, number and the holder's date of birth; it does not search by plate.
PV - posvidchennia vodiia, the driving licence
The service runs on the open-data portal of the Main Service Centre of the MVS (HSC)

safety.title: Crash safety statistics
safety.unavailable: Safety ratings aren't available right now.
safety.none: No NHTSA rating found - this US-market database rarely covers EU/JDM-spec or Soviet-era vehicles.
safety.coverageNhtsa: Covers vehicles sold new in the US, matched by exact make/model/year. Only reliably covers MY2011 onward (NHTSA's current combined 5-star program) - older model years used different, non-comparable test criteria.
safety.source: Source: NHTSA 5-Star Safety Ratings (USA) - matched by make/model/year, US-spec trims only.
safety.euroncapNone: No Euro NCAP rating found for this make/model.
safety.coverageEuroncap: Covers EU-spec vehicles Euro NCAP actually tested, 2017 onward. A rating expires 6 years after publication (shown as "other tested generations" past that point).
safety.euroncapNoGenerationMatch: No rating matches this vehicle's model year - other tested generations are shown below.
safety.euroncapExpired: This rating has expired (Euro NCAP ratings are valid for 6 years from publication).
safety.euroncapSource: Source: Euro NCAP - matched by make/model, EU-spec vehicles.
safety.euroncapRatingsInfoStars: 0–5 stars: Euro NCAP's overall safety rating for this tested variant.
safety.euroncapRatingsInfoAdultOccupant: Adult Occupant: how well the structure and restraints protect adult occupants in a crash.
safety.euroncapRatingsInfoChildOccupant: Child Occupant: protection for children in the car's own child seats, plus how easy it is to fit compatible child seats.
safety.euroncapRatingsInfoVulnerableRoad: Vulnerable Road Users: protection for pedestrians and cyclists struck by the car, and how well its systems detect them.
safety.euroncapRatingsInfoSafetyAssist: Safety Assist: how much standard-fit tech (autonomous braking, lane assist, speed limiting) helps avoid a crash in the first place.
safety.euroncapRatingsInfoSafetyPack: Safety Pack: results for an optional equipment package - the base/Standard trim may score differently.
safety.euroncapRatingsInfoExpiry: Ratings expire after 6 years - Euro NCAP's test protocol gets stricter over time, so an old 5-star rating isn't directly comparable to a new one.
safety.jncapNone: No JNCAP rating found for this make/model - this Japan-domestic database only covers vehicles NASVA actually tested.
safety.coverageJncap: Covers JDM-domestic vehicles NASVA actually tested, 2003 onward (with real gaps: no 2004-2006 or 2008).
safety.jncapNoGenerationMatch: No rating matches this vehicle's model year - other tested generations are shown below.
safety.jncapSource: Source: JNCAP (Japan, NASVA) - matched by make/model, JDM-domestic vehicles.
safety.jncapRatingsInfoStars: 0–5 stars: JNCAP's overall safety rating for this tested vehicle.
safety.jncapRatingsInfoPreventive: Preventive safety: how well the car's active-safety tech (autonomous braking, lane assist, headlights) helps avoid a crash - graded A (best) through E.
safety.jncapRatingsInfoCollision: Collision safety: occupant and pedestrian protection in frontal, side, and whiplash tests - graded A (best) through E.
safety.jncapRatingsInfoEmergencyCall: Emergency call system: whether the car automatically alerts emergency services after a serious crash, and how advanced that system is.
safety.cncapNone: No C-NCAP rating found for this make/model - this China-market database only covers vehicles CATARC actually tested.
safety.coverageCncap: Covers China-market vehicles CATARC actually tested, 2006 onward.
safety.cncapNoGenerationMatch: No rating matches this vehicle's model year - other tested generations are shown below.
safety.cncapSource: Source: C-NCAP (China, CATARC) - matched by make/model, China-market vehicles.
safety.cncapRatingsInfoUnit: C-NCAP has no star rating - scores before 2018 are raw points with no fixed maximum, and scores from 2018 onward are a clean percentage; the two are never directly comparable.
safety.cncapRatingsInfoOccupant: Occupant protection: how well the structure and restraints protect occupants in a crash.
safety.cncapRatingsInfoVru: Pedestrian/VRU protection: protection for pedestrians and cyclists struck by the car (tested from 2018 onward only).
safety.cncapRatingsInfoActiveSafety: Active safety: how much standard-fit tech helps avoid a crash in the first place (tested from 2018 onward only).
safety.kncapNone: No KNCAP rating found for this make/model - this Korea-market database only covers vehicles KNCAP actually tested.
safety.coverageKncap: Covers Korea-market vehicles KNCAP actually tested, 2021 onward - an older historical corpus exists but isn't in this database yet.
safety.kncapNoGenerationMatch: No rating matches this vehicle's model year - other tested generations are shown below.
safety.kncapSource: Source: KNCAP (Korea, MOLIT/KoROAD) - matched by make/model, Korea-market vehicles, 2021 onward only.
safety.kncapRatingsInfoClass: Class (1-5): KNCAP's overall safety tier for this tested vehicle - 1 is the best.
safety.kncapRatingsInfoCrash: Crash safety: occupant protection in frontal, side, and pole-impact tests.
safety.kncapRatingsInfoPedestrian: Pedestrian safety: protection for pedestrians struck by the car.
safety.kncapRatingsInfoAccident: Accident-prevention safety: how much standard-fit tech helps avoid a crash in the first place.
safety.iihsNone: No IIHS rating found for this make/model - this US-market database only covers vehicles IIHS actually tested.
safety.coverageIihs: Covers US-market vehicles IIHS actually tested, model year 1994 onward.
safety.iihsNoGenerationMatch: No rating matches this vehicle's model year.
safety.iihsSource: Source: IIHS (US, insurance-industry-funded) - matched by make/model, US-market vehicles, model year 1994 onward only.
safety.iihsRatingsInfoScale: Good/Acceptable/Marginal/Poor: IIHS's crashworthiness scale across small-overlap front, moderate-overlap front, side, and headlight tests.
safety.iihsRatingsInfoFcp: Front crash prevention: Superior/Advanced/Basic on older tests, or Good/Acceptable/Marginal/Poor on newer ones - how well standard-fit tech helps avoid a crash.
safety.iihsRatingsInfoAward: Top Safety Pick / Top Safety Pick+: IIHS's annual award for vehicles meeting its highest combined standards that model year.
safety.coverageInfoIntro: All six sources are supplementary, best-effort matches - none of them guarantees a result for every car, so always check the vehicle's actual specification.
safety.coverageInfoEuroNcapBody: Tests EU-spec cars - the vast majority of Ukraine's registered fleet by brand - but only specific tested trims and generations, not every model or year. A rating only shows up when Euro NCAP actually tested that make/model.
safety.brandsInfoIntro: NHTSA only tests vehicles sold new in the US, matched by exact make/model/year - not every model or year of a covered brand has a rating on file.
safety.brandsInfoDiscontinued: Discontinued in the US (older model years only)
safety.brandsInfoUncovered: Never sold in the US - no rating will ever exist, e.g.
safety.coverageInfoJncapBody: Tests JDM-domestic cars - models never exported to the EU or US, like the Toyota Alphard/Crown/Mark X or Nissan Skyline/Cedric/Elgrand. Only vehicles NASVA actually tested have a rating.
safety.coverageInfoCncapBody: Tests China-market cars - the BYD/Geely/Chery/Zeekr/Haval fleet Ukraine grey-imports in volume - under their China-spec names, translated here from CATARC's own Chinese-language results. Only vehicles CATARC actually tested have a rating.
safety.coverageInfoKncapBody: Tests Korea-domestic cars - Hyundai/Kia/Genesis/KGM EVs and other Korea-only models - under their Korean names, translated here from KNCAP's own results. Only covers 2021 onward, and only vehicles KNCAP actually tested have a rating.
safety.coverageInfoIihsBody: Tests the same US-spec fleet NHTSA does, but on a different methodology (Good/Acceptable/Marginal/Poor across small-overlap, side, and crash-prevention tests, plus Top Safety Pick awards) - a car can rate well on one scale and not the other. Only vehicles IIHS actually tested have a rating.
safety.ratingsInfoStars: 1–5 stars, more stars = safer. "Not Rated" means NHTSA never tested that specific trim.
safety.ratingsInfoOverall: Overall: a combined score across all frontal, side, and rollover tests below.
safety.ratingsInfoFront: Front: driver/passenger protection in a 35 mph frontal crash into a fixed barrier.
safety.ratingsInfoSide: Side: occupant protection in a 38 mph side impact, plus a separate side pole impact test.
safety.ratingsInfoAverage: Average: when a make/model/year has several tested trims (body style, drivetrain), this is the mean across all of them, shown above the individual breakdown.
safety.ratingsInfoRollover: Rollover: risk of a rollover in a single-vehicle loss-of-control event - more stars = lower risk.
safety.ratingsInfoSidePole: Side pole: a separate, more severe side-impact test against a narrow pole (like a tree or post).
safety.ratingsInfoRolloverRisk: Rollover risk %: the actual estimated probability of a rollover, behind the star rating - plus the dynamic test result (e.g. "No Tip") from a real avoidance-maneuver test.
safety.ratingsInfoEquipment: ESC/FCW/LDW: whether stability control, forward-collision warning, and lane-departure warning came standard, optional, or weren't offered on this trim.
safety.ratingsInfoCombinedSideBarrier: Side barrier (combined): an older/secondary side-impact sub-score alongside the main Side and Side pole ratings above.
safety.ratingsInfoComplaints: Complaints/recalls: lifetime counts reported to NHTSA for this vehicle - not part of the crash test itself.
safety.ratingsInfoInvestigations: Investigations: open or closed NHTSA safety investigations into this vehicle.

about.heading: About
about.p1: This app provides vehicle data since January 2013.
about.p2: The information about the vehicles and their owners is taken from the single state open data portal data.gov.ua, managed by the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Ukraine.
about.p3: The single state open data portal was created at the request of the Law of Ukraine “On Access to Public Information” and the Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine of October 21, 2015 No. 835 “On Approval of the Regulations on Data Sets to be Disclosed in the Form of Open Data”.
about.p4: The portal is intended to provide access to public information in the form of open data and provides access to information from authorities with the possibility of its subsequent use.
about.p5: Anyone may freely copy, publish, distribute and use public information in the form of open data, including for commercial purposes and in combination with other information or one's own product, provided there is a mandatory link to the source of such information.
about.plateNotice: Since May 2026 (plates are in the database for January 2013 – 29 April 2026), a Ministry of Internal Affairs order (№ 67/ОД) has stopped the portal from publishing plate numbers for new registrations. Where possible, this app reconstructs a vehicle's plate from its own VIN's earlier registration history - such entries are marked as reconstructed.

legal.privacy.heading: Privacy policy
legal.privacy.intro: Cars UA (carsua.app) is a free lookup tool built on public open data. This page explains what the app stores about you.
legal.privacy.registry.p: Plate, VIN and vehicle details come from the public registry on data.gov.ua. The registry we use does not contain owners' names or contact details, and we do not try to identify owners. Searches you run are used only to return a result.
legal.privacy.device.p: Search history, favorites, language, theme and optional offline data are kept in your browser's local storage and never leave your device. You can clear them at any time from your browser settings. We do not use advertising cookies.
legal.privacy.account.p: Signing in is optional. If you sign in with Google, we store your email address, display name and profile picture URL; if you sign in with Telegram, we store your Telegram numeric id, display name and profile picture URL (we receive no email or phone number). This runs your account and its saved settings. We never see your Google password or Telegram login code. You can delete your saved settings yourself in Settings, and ask us to delete your account and all its data at any time.
legal.privacy.thirdParty.p: When enabled, PostHog (anonymous usage statistics) and Sentry (error reports) receive technical data such as pages visited, browser type and error details. Embedded content (YouTube, Sketchfab, Google Maps) and translation or VIN-decoding requests are handled by their providers under their own policies. The site runs on a Contabo virtual server behind Cloudflare; regular backups, which include account data, are kept in Cloudflare R2 storage, and email is sent through Resend.
legal.privacy.rights.p: You can use the app without an account, clear local data in your browser, and request deletion of your account. Changes to this policy are published on this page.
legal.terms.heading: Terms of use
legal.terms.intro: By using Cars UA you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, please do not use the service.
legal.terms.use.p: Cars UA is provided free of charge for personal and informational use. The source code is available under the MIT license (see About).
legal.terms.data.p: Data comes from open government and third-party sources and may be incomplete, outdated or wrong, and some records are reconstructed. Values and estimates are indicative only. Do not rely on the app for purchases, legal, insurance or safety decisions without checking official sources.
legal.terms.conduct.p: Do not use the service to harass or track individuals, to break the law, or to overload it with automated requests. We may limit access to protect the service.
legal.terms.liability.p: The service is provided 'as is' without warranties of any kind. To the extent permitted by law, the authors are not liable for any loss arising from using the app or relying on its data.
legal.terms.changes.p: We may update the service and these terms. Continued use after changes means you accept them.

vdb.info.title: Cross-market data
vdb.info.lead: Facts from VehiclesDB, an open catalog built from the official vehicle registers of 15 countries (Ukraine included). Matched to the catalog model: {{name}}.
vdb.info.crossMake: Sold under another make - the catalog lists this model as {{name}}: the same car, badged differently in other markets.
vdb.info.loose: Approximate match - the registry's model name only starts with, or contains, the catalog name, so other generations or variants of that model may differ.
vdb.info.alsoSold: Also sold in - registers other than Ukraine's where this model appears: {{countries}}.
vdb.info.decile: Top {{band}}% of models - where the model ranks among all models in the countries it is registered in (the {{count}} markets: {{markets}}). 10% is the most popular tenth. It is the average of each country's own ranking, every country weighing the same - so it is not a Ukrainian rank, and Europe counts more because most covered registers are European.
vdb.info.uaOnly: Sold only in Ukraine's register - no other covered register lists this model.
vdb.info.rare: Rare in other markets - it ranks in the bottom third (decile 8 or lower) of the markets that list it, even if it is common in Ukraine.

rdw.title: Specs
rdw.scaleHint: Typical passenger-car scale: {{scale}}. The dot is the model's median, the shaded part its min–max.
rdw.footnote: Typical figures for the {{name}} as registered in the Netherlands, based on {{n}} vehicles first registered in {{year}}. A Ukrainian-market build may differ.
rdw.info.lead: RDW is the Rijksdienst voor het Wegverkeer - the Netherlands Vehicle Authority, which keeps the Dutch vehicle register and approves vehicle types. This block shows typical power, engine capacity, unladen mass and CO₂ of the {{name}} from that register (open data). The main figure is the median; “range” is the lowest to highest value among the vehicles. Where the register records them, it also gives gross mass, towing limits, seats, doors, dimensions and top speed.
rdw.info.sample: Based on {{n}} vehicles first registered in the Netherlands in {{year}}.
rdw.info.nearYear: There is no data for this exact model year - the nearest year with data, {{year}}, is shown.
rdw.info.loose: Approximate match - the registry’s model name only starts with, or contains, the Dutch model name, so other generations or variants of that model may differ.
rdw.info.crossMake: Sold under another make in the Netherlands - the Dutch register lists this model as {{name}}.
rdw.info.spread: These are EU-spec figures. A car imported to Ukraine from another market, or with a different engine or trim, can differ - check the vehicle documents.
rdw.info.co2: CO₂ is the type-approval figure: WLTP where the vehicle has it, otherwise the older NEDC. It is absent for electric cars.
rdw.info.credit: Data from RDW open data (CC0), opendata.rdw.nl.

recalls.info.model: A campaign covers the vehicles a producer built to a given specification. It cannot tell whether this particular car is affected, and a Ukrainian car may be built to another specification or already repaired. Check the VIN with the producer or an authorised dealer.

recalls.what.title: What is a recall campaign?
recalls.what.body: A recall campaign is when a vehicle maker (usually together with the safety authority) calls back every car built to a certain specification to fix a defect that may be unsafe, free of charge, at an authorised dealer. The lists below are what the Dutch authority RDW (EU) and the US authority NHTSA have published for this model.
recalls.what.ukraine: How it relates to Ukraine: we found no comparable open recall register for Ukraine. Most Ukrainian cars are imported from the EU or US, so a campaign for the same model is a useful warning, but it may not apply to your build, and the car may already have been fixed abroad. Only the VIN tells: ask an official dealer of the brand or the producer.
nhtsa.marketHint: Recall campaigns filed with NHTSA, the US vehicle-safety authority, for this model year. US-market vehicles only; not an EU or Ukrainian list.
nhtsa.footnote: NHTSA lists {{count}} recall campaign(s) for {{name}} in the United States. These are campaigns for the model year, not a check of this car, and a US-spec car can differ from yours.
nhtsa.ota: fixed by a software update over the air
nhtsa.about.summary: What is wrong and which vehicles are covered, as the producer reported it to NHTSA (original English).
nhtsa.about.consequence: What can happen if the defect is not fixed, in the producer's words (original English).
nhtsa.about.remedy: What the producer does to fix it - usually a free repair at a dealer in the US (original English).
nhtsa.about.advisory: Warnings NHTSA attaches to some campaigns: a "do not drive" order, advice to park outside because of a fire risk, or a fix delivered as a software update.
nhtsa.about.code: NHTSA's own number for the campaign; quote it when looking the campaign up on nhtsa.gov.
nhtsa.info.credit: US data: NHTSA open data (public domain), api.nhtsa.gov. Campaigns are for US-market vehicles of this model year and may not apply to your build.
nhtsa.complaints.title: Owner complaints
nhtsa.complaints.info: Complaints are reports that US owners filed with NHTSA. They are unverified and are not findings or recalls; a large model gets more of them simply because more were sold. Only the counts are shown here, never the owners' texts.
nhtsa.complaints.components: Most-named parts (a complaint can name several):
nhtsa.about.component: NHTSA files each recall under a component (the part of the car concerned), from a fixed list, then narrows it down after colons. The heading is translated; this line is NHTSA’s original wording.
recalls.about.category: The part of the vehicle the defect is in, as classified by RDW.
recalls.about.defect: What is wrong with the part, as RDW words it.
recalls.about.consequences: What can happen if the defect is not fixed, in the producer's and RDW's words (original Dutch).
recalls.about.hazards: The kind of danger RDW assigns to the campaign: accident with injury, higher injury risk, fire, or environmental harm.
recalls.about.remedy: What the producer does to fix it - usually the owner is invited to a dealer who replaces or repairs the part for free (original Dutch).
recalls.about.vehicles: How many vehicles the producer included in the campaign worldwide and, if reported, in the Netherlands.
recalls.about.code: RDW's own reference for the campaign; quote it when looking the campaign up on rdw.nl.
recalls.cat.typeApproval: Product does not meet type-approval requirements
recalls.hazard.higherInjury: Higher risk of injury in an accident
rdw.smallSample: Small sample: only {{n}} vehicles - treat these figures as a rough guide.
rdw.info.approx: All figures are approximate. They describe typical Dutch-registered vehicles of this model and year, not this particular car: engine versions, trims, imports and later modifications differ, which is why a range is shown next to the median.
rdw.info.small: Small sample: the figures come from only {{n}} vehicles. A few unusual cars (a grey import, a rare engine) can move the median and the range a lot, so use them as a rough guide only.
rdw.marketHint: RDW (Rijksdienst voor het Wegverkeer) - the Netherlands Vehicle Authority. EU-spec figures from the Dutch vehicle register.
rdw.about.power:
Peak engine power in kilowatts (kW), with horsepower (hp) in brackets - 1 kW ≈ 1.36 hp. The main figure is the median of the Dutch vehicles of this model and year; “range” is the lowest to highest, because engine versions differ. For an electric car it is the peak electric motor power; for a hybrid, the combustion engine alone.
50 kW - ≈ 68 hp
100 kW - ≈ 136 hp
150 kW - ≈ 204 hp
rdw.about.displacement: Engine displacement - the total volume of all cylinders, in cubic centimetres (cm³, “cc”). Median of the Dutch vehicles of this model and year; “range” shows the engine versions sold. Absent for electric cars. “This car (registry)” is what the Ukrainian registry says about this exact vehicle - compare the two.
rdw.about.mass: Unladen mass (“massa ledig voertuig”) - the empty vehicle ready to drive, without driver, passengers or cargo, in kilograms (kg). It is close to the “kerb weight” in the basic section, but measured by the Dutch authority; small differences are normal (equipment, fuel level, how it is counted).
rdw.about.co2:
Combined tailpipe CO₂ in grams per kilometre (g/km), from type approval: WLTP where the vehicle has it, otherwise the older NEDC test. Real-world use is higher. Absent for electric cars.
Why it can differ from the Emissions section below: that section shows EPA / EEA reference data filtered by this car’s own fuel and engine size, and a range of the matching entries. This one is the median and range of ALL Dutch-registered vehicles of the model and year - every engine, diesel and hybrid versions, imports - and some are measured with WLTP, others with NEDC (WLTP gives higher numbers). Different source, different sample: when they disagree, trust the one that matches your engine; the Emissions section is the closer one.
rdw.about.topSpeed: Maximum design speed (“maximale constructiesnelheid”) in km/h, as recorded at type approval. Many cars have no value recorded in the Dutch register, so this row appears only when enough vehicles of the model have one. Not the speed you can legally drive, and electronic limiters may lower it.
rdw.about.grossMass: Permitted maximum (gross) mass - “toegestane maximum massa” - the most the vehicle may weigh fully loaded: the unladen mass plus driver, passengers, fuel and cargo. Shown in kilograms (kg) with tonnes (t) in brackets. Compare with the unladen mass above; the difference is the payload. The registry’s own figure, when it has one, is shown underneath.
rdw.about.towBraked: Maximum mass of a trailer with its own brakes that the vehicle may tow, in kg. A type-approval limit; the tow bar, local rules and your driving licence category may allow less.
rdw.about.towUnbraked: Maximum mass of a trailer without its own brakes that the vehicle may tow, in kg. A type-approval limit; the tow bar, local rules and your driving licence category may allow less.
rdw.about.seats: Number of seats including the driver, as approved for the Dutch register. Variants of a model (a 7-seat version, a van with a second row) can differ.
rdw.about.doors: Number of doors as recorded in the Dutch register. Whether the tailgate counts depends on how the type was approved, so a 5-door hatchback is sometimes listed with 4.
rdw.about.length: Overall vehicle length in centimetres (cm), with metres (m) in brackets. The Dutch register records dimensions for only a part of the cars, so this row appears only when enough vehicles of the model have a value.
rdw.about.width: Overall vehicle width in centimetres (cm), with metres (m) in brackets, usually without the door mirrors. Shown only when enough vehicles of the model have a value in the Dutch register.
rdw.about.height: Overall vehicle height in centimetres (cm), with metres (m) in brackets, of the empty vehicle. Shown only when enough vehicles of the model have a value in the Dutch register.
rdw.about.wheelbase: Wheelbase - the distance between the front and rear axles - in centimetres (cm), with metres (m) in brackets. A longer wheelbase usually means more rear legroom and a smoother ride; versions of one model with different body lengths differ. Rule of thumb: under 250 cm is a small city car, 250–270 compact, 270–290 mid-size/family, over 290 large (big SUV, van). It is not tied to ground clearance - a long car can sit low.
rdw.priceExTax: New price in NL, excl. VAT and BPM
value.title: Estimated value
value.chipHint: Rough estimate: EU value plus Ukrainian customs. Not a market price
value.info.lead: “Est. value” chip: a rough estimate from the EU new price, not a market price, not a Ukrainian price.
value.info.how: The Dutch new list price of the {{name}} is about {{price}}. At age {{age}} a car keeps about {{percent}} % of its new price on the assumed depreciation curve, which gives the range above.
value.info.rough: Small sample: the new price comes from only {{n}} Dutch vehicles, so this is an even rougher guess.
value.tip: {{ua}} in Ukraine with customs paid; {{eu}} before customs, from the Dutch new price of ~{{n}} vehicles first registered in {{year}}. Not a market price.
value.info.nearYear: No data for the exact model year, so the nearest one ({{year}}) is used.
value.info.floor: Old cars: the depreciation table ends at about {{years}} years, after which we assume the car keeps {{percent}} % of its new price - our own assumption, not part of the source, so the figure is very rough. The older the car, the wider the range, because one example can be a wreck or a collector's piece.
value.fuel.title: New price by version (fuel)
value.fuel.note: Median list price of the Dutch cars of this model and year per fuel version, and the same curve applied to each. The chip uses all versions together; if this car is a different version, read its row. Dimmed rows rest on very few cars.
value.info.range: The range is ±{{percent}} % around the estimate: mileage, condition, trim and the Ukrainian market can move a real price well outside it. Shown only for a well-sampled model and while the curve still has a value for the age.
value.info.credit: Prices: RDW open data (CC0). Depreciation curve: the Dutch BPM forfaitaire afschrijvingstabel (Belastingdienst), an official tax schedule, not market prices.
value.chart.newPrice: New price in the Netherlands by model year
value.chart.byAge: Estimated value by age (this car marked)
about.source.belastingdienst: Belastingdienst (Dutch Tax Administration) - the BPM forfaitaire depreciation table, used as the assumed curve of how much of the new price a car keeps with age in the rough value estimate.
rdw.info.price: The price row is the Dutch NEW list price (“catalogusprijs”) in euros. It includes 21 % Dutch VAT and the BPM registration tax, so it is not a Ukrainian price and not a resale value; the “excl. VAT and BPM” row removes both.
rdw.info.fuelMix: Fuel mix, body type, colours and energy label are shares of the Dutch vehicles of this model and year; the consumption, noise and electric figures cover only the vehicles that have them, and the row is hidden when too few do.
rdw.about.price:
The NEW list price of the vehicle in the Netherlands (“catalogusprijs”), in euros: the median of the Dutch vehicles of this model and year, with the cheapest to most expensive version as the range, rounded to 100 €.
It INCLUDES 21 % Dutch VAT and the BPM registration tax (see the next rows), so it is neither a Ukrainian price nor what the car is worth now. Shown only when the register has the price for enough vehicles.
rdw.about.priceExTax: The Dutch new list price with 21 % VAT and the BPM registration tax taken out: price ÷ 1.21 − BPM. A rough “price before Dutch taxes”. Where no BPM is recorded (electric cars are exempt) only the VAT is removed.
rdw.about.bpm: BPM (“belasting van personenauto’s en motorrijwielen”) - the Dutch tax on a new car that grows with CO₂ emissions and is included in the list price. Electric cars are mostly exempt, so this row is absent for them.
rdw.about.kerbMass: Kerb mass (“massa rijklaar”) - the vehicle ready to drive including a 75 kg driver, fluids and a mostly full tank. About 75 kg more than the unladen mass.
rdw.about.cylinders: Number of engine cylinders. Absent for electric cars.
rdw.about.consumption: Combined fuel consumption in litres per 100 km from type approval: WLTP where the vehicle has it, otherwise the older NEDC. Real-world use is higher. For plug-in hybrids it is the weighted figure. A model sold with petrol, diesel and hybrid engines mixes them here - see the fuel mix.
rdw.about.evKwh: Electric energy use of battery-electric cars in kWh per 100 km (WLTP where available), at the plug - a lower figure means a more efficient car. Only vehicles with a recorded value count.
rdw.about.evRange: Electric range of battery-electric cars in kilometres from the WLTP test (older cars: the earlier test, which was more optimistic). Real-world range is lower, especially in winter and at motorway speed.
rdw.about.noise: Drive-by noise in decibels (dB) measured at type approval, 7.5 m from the car. Every +3 dB is roughly a doubling of sound energy. Shown only when enough vehicles of the model have a value.
rdw.about.fuelMix: How the Dutch vehicles of this model and year split by fuel: petrol, diesel, electric, hybrid (including mild hybrids), plug-in hybrid and gas. It explains why power, consumption and CO₂ can span a wide range - they mix these versions. Classes under 2 % are not shown.
rdw.about.bodyTypes: The most common body types of the Dutch vehicles of this model and year, as classified by the register (estate, hatchback, MPV …). A model name often covers more than one body, e.g. hatchback and estate.
rdw.about.colours: The most common colours of the Dutch vehicles of this model and year (first colour in the register). A guide to what was bought in the Netherlands, not to what exists in Ukraine.
rdw.about.energyLabels: The Dutch energy label (A best … G worst) the vehicle got at registration, from CO₂ and fuel use. Only assigned to cars with a fuel-based figure, so electric and older cars often have none; shown as shares of those that have one.
about.source.rdw: RDW (Rijksdienst voor het Wegverkeer, the Netherlands Vehicle Authority) - EU-spec power, engine capacity, unladen mass and CO₂ per make, model and year, aggregated from the Dutch vehicle register, plus EU recall campaigns (open data, CC0).
about.source.ev: Open EV Data (OpenChargingCloud, MIT licence, © 2019 Niklas Hösl) - usable battery, consumption and AC / DC charging of electric and plug-in hybrid models, as of 2020.

stats.vdb.title: Markets: how popular are registered cars elsewhere?
stats.vdb.info:
Registry passenger cars matched to VehiclesDB, an open catalog built from the official vehicle registers of 15 countries (Ukraine included).
Share of cars by band - each model has a popularity decile: the average of its own ranking in every country that lists it, equal weight per country. Top 10% is the most popular tenth of models. Europe counts more because most covered registers are European.
Common here, rare elsewhere - models with at least 1,000 cars here that rank in the bottom third of the markets listing them; the flags are those other markets.
Only in Ukraine - models that appear in no other covered register.
Cars the catalog cannot match (trucks, trailers, unusual spellings) are left out of every figure except the coverage line.

section.about.fuelSummary:
Fuel use and CO₂ of the passenger cars in the registry.
Fleet average - mean tailpipe CO₂ (g/km) of the cars that got an estimate, weighted by registrations
Cars with an estimate - the share of passenger cars we could match to a similar reference vehicle; the rest are left out of every number on this page
Passenger cars - all passenger cars in the registry
Sources - registry data from data.gov.ua; reference CO₂ from EEA (official EU type-approval, WLTP) and EPA (US fuel-economy database)
section.about.fuelPowertrain:
Passenger cars grouped by the fuel written in the registry (petrol, diesel, gas, electric, hybrid…); click a row for the details.
Hybrid / plug-in - one group, because the registry text cannot tell them apart
Drill-down - the top 50 models and top 30 brands of the class, the rarest models (at least 5 cars, single cars are mostly registry noise) and the share of each model year since 2000
Not included - trucks, buses, motorcycles and other non-passenger vehicles
Sources - registry fuel field (data.gov.ua); average CO₂ from EEA / EPA reference data
section.about.fuelChart:
Average tailpipe CO₂ (g/km) of the matched cars, by model year, brand or fuel class. Lower is cleaner.
How it is computed - each registry car is matched to similar reference vehicles (same make and model, a model year within 3, a similar engine size), weighted by registrations; one source is used per estimate, EU (EEA) before US (EPA)
Included - model years from 1990, brands with at least 2000 matched cars
Not included - cars with no match; different test cycles (WLTP / NEDC / EPA) are mixed, so treat it as a rough comparison
Sources - data.gov.ua registry; EEA and EPA reference data
section.about.fuelModels:
The models with the lowest and highest average CO₂ (g/km), top 5 (expandable).
Included - models with at least 1500 cars matched to reference data
Not included - rarer models, and cars with no match; so a famously clean or dirty model can be missing if it is rare here
Sources - data.gov.ua registry; EEA and EPA reference data
section.about.fuelDistribution:
How many matched cars fall into each CO₂ band (g/km); bar colours follow the same green-to-red scale as the CO₂ badge on a car page.
Not included - cars with no reference match
Sources - data.gov.ua registry; EEA and EPA reference data
section.about.safetySummary:
Crash-test results of the passenger cars in the registry.
Fleet average - mean combined crash score (0–100, higher is safer) of the rated cars, weighted by registrations
Cars with a rating - the share of passenger cars we could match to a crash-tested model; the rest are left out of every number on this page
Passenger cars - all passenger cars in the registry
Sources - registry data from data.gov.ua; ratings from Euro NCAP, JNCAP, C-NCAP, KNCAP and IIHS
section.about.safetyChart:
Average combined crash score, by model year, brand or rating source.
How it is computed - every programme’s result is converted to a 0–100 scale and averaged over the programmes that rated a similar car (same make and model, a close model year), weighted by registrations
By source - the bar is that programme’s own average; the percentage is how much of the fleet it covers
Included - model years from 1990, brands with at least 2000 rated cars
Not included - cars with no rating. The programmes test differently, so this is a rough comparison, not an official rating
Sources - data.gov.ua registry; Euro NCAP, JNCAP, C-NCAP, KNCAP, IIHS
section.about.safetyModels:
The models with the highest and lowest combined crash score, top 5 (expandable).
Included - models with at least 1500 rated cars
Not included - rarer models and models that no programme has tested; a low rank can also mean an old test of an older generation
Sources - data.gov.ua registry; Euro NCAP, JNCAP, C-NCAP, KNCAP, IIHS
section.about.safetyDistribution:
How many rated cars fall into each crash-score band (0–100); bars use the same green-to-red scale as the badges on a car page.
Not included - cars with no rating
Sources - data.gov.ua registry; Euro NCAP, JNCAP, C-NCAP, KNCAP, IIHS
section.about.statsSummary:
Totals over the registry data loaded from the state open-data portal (data.gov.ua).
Total registration actions - every row in the registry: first registrations, re-registrations, deregistrations, so one car can appear several times
Distinct plates - different plate numbers seen, each counted once
Distinct VINs - different cars (by VIN), each counted once
Plateless - rows with no plate since the 2026 plate removal (order №67/ОД); such cars are identified by VIN only
Sources - State open-data portal data.gov.ua - the vehicle registrations dataset published by the Ministry of Internal Affairs service centres, loaded into our database
section.about.statsTopBrand:
The makes with the most distinct plates in the registry. Counts are cars, not registration actions, so a car sold many times counts once. Only makes the registry names are listed; unknown or blank makes are skipped.
Sources - State open-data portal data.gov.ua - the vehicle registrations dataset published by the Ministry of Internal Affairs service centres, loaded into our database
section.about.statsTopModel:
The make + model pairs with the most distinct plates. Spellings of the same model (ZAZ / Daewoo / Chevrolet Lanos, Sens…) are folded into one row. Models with no recorded name are not listed.
Sources - State open-data portal data.gov.ua - the vehicle registrations dataset published by the Ministry of Internal Affairs service centres, loaded into our database
section.about.statsTopColor:
The colours with the most distinct plates, as written in the registry. Cars with no colour recorded are not counted here.
Sources - State open-data portal data.gov.ua - the vehicle registrations dataset published by the Ministry of Internal Affairs service centres, loaded into our database
section.about.statsTopRegion:
The regions with the most distinct plates. The region comes from the plate prefix, so plateless cars (2026 onwards) and online-service plates (ДІ / ЕД series, which belong to no region) are not counted.
Sources - State open-data portal data.gov.ua - the vehicle registrations dataset published by the Ministry of Internal Affairs service centres, loaded into our database; plate prefix → region table from the official plate-code statute
section.about.statsWeight:
The registered models with the highest and lowest unladen mass, by vehicle group (All, passenger, truck, bus, motorcycle, trailer, other).
Where it comes from - the registry's own weight field; for passenger cars that the Dutch RDW database recognises, RDW's typical mass is used instead, which is more reliable
What is listed - models with at least a few hundred registered vehicles; the figure is the model's typical range edge (1st / 99th percentile), so one mistyped record cannot top the list
What is not - rare models below that floor, and records with an impossible weight (lighter than a car can be, or lighter than a fair share of its own gross weight)
Sources - State open-data portal data.gov.ua - the vehicle registrations dataset published by the Ministry of Internal Affairs service centres, loaded into our database; RDW open data (opendata.rdw.nl) - the Dutch vehicle authority
section.about.statsOrigin:
Passenger cars currently registered in Ukraine, split by the home country of the brand and by the country the VIN says the car was assembled in.
Where it comes from - brand country and history from Wikidata; assembly country from the first three VIN characters (NHTSA vPIC list plus a curated table)
How it is counted - by the car's model year, so a 1985 Skoda is Czechoslovakia and a 2005 one is the Czech Republic; Soviet-built cars count as the USSR
What is not - cars with a non-standard VIN (mostly older ones) and brands we could not match are counted as unknown; the assembly country is brand and plant level, not a guarantee about one car; the registry does not record the country a used car was imported from
Sources - State open-data portal data.gov.ua; Wikidata (CC0); NHTSA vPIC
section.about.statsSpec:
Passenger-car models with the highest and lowest value of one specification.
Power, Engine - from the registry's own columns (5th / 95th percentile of each model, to ignore typos); pure electric cars have no real engine size, so they are skipped in the Engine ranking
Height, Length - typical values from the Dutch RDW database, or from the model's Wikipedia generations when RDW has none
Fuel tank - from Wikipedia only, so only a handful of models are ranked for now
What is listed - models with at least a few hundred registered vehicles that we could match to a source. Models we could not match are not ranked
Vans filed as cars in the registry (Crafter, Transit…) rank as cars
Sources - State open-data portal data.gov.ua - the vehicle registrations dataset published by the Ministry of Internal Affairs service centres, loaded into our database; RDW open data (opendata.rdw.nl) - the Dutch vehicle authority; Wikipedia - model generation specifications
section.about.statsTable:
The full registry, grouped by the tab you pick (region, year, make, colour, fuel…).
Total rows - registration actions, so a car registered several times counts several times
Distinct plates / Distinct VINs - each plate or car counted once
The map shows the same numbers per region; the region is read from the plate prefix, so plateless cars and online-service plates are missing from it
Sources - State open-data portal data.gov.ua - the vehicle registrations dataset published by the Ministry of Internal Affairs service centres, loaded into our database; plate prefix → region table from the official plate-code statute

install.heading: Install the app
install.intro: Cars UA is a PWA (progressive web app): the website that installs like an app - its own icon, its own window, no app store.
install.alreadyInstalled: ✓ You are using the installed app.
install.iosHint: On iPhone/iPad there is no install button: open this site in Safari, tap Share, then “Add to Home Screen”.
install.noPrompt: Your browser has not offered installation (yet). Use the steps below, or open the site in Chrome, Edge or Safari over HTTPS.
install.step.android: Android (Chrome): menu ⋮ → “Install app” / “Add to Home screen”.
install.step.desktop: Desktop (Chrome, Edge): the install icon at the right end of the address bar, or menu → “Install Cars UA”.
install.what.h: What a PWA is and what it can do
install.what.1: A regular website plus a manifest (name, icons, colours) and a service worker (a script that sits between the page and the network).
install.what.2: Installable: a home-screen or desktop icon, a standalone window without browser chrome, an entry in the app switcher.
install.what.3: Works offline and loads fast, because the app shell and data are kept on the device.
install.what.4: Other possibilities (not used here): push notifications, background sync, badges, share target, app shortcuts, file handlers.
install.what.5: One codebase for every platform and no store review; updates ship the moment you reload.
install.ours.h: What the Cars UA app does
install.ours.1: The app shell (pages, scripts, styles) is saved on first visit, so the app opens without a network.
install.ours.2: Plates and VINs you have searched, with their specs, safety, fuel and reviews data, are kept on the device (a capped number per kind). Favorites are never dropped by the cap.
install.ours.3: Car photos, logos and backgrounds you have seen are cached as images.
install.ours.4: An offline banner shows when the connection is gone; saved results are marked “offline”.
install.ours.5: When a new version is ready you get an “Update” prompt - nothing is swapped under you mid-session.
install.ours.6: The installed app asks the browser to protect its storage from automatic cleanup.
install.limits.1: Offline you only get what you opened before. A new plate or VIN needs the internet - the registry is not stored on the device.
install.limits.2: Online-only: AR/camera scan, PDF and DOCX export, the news/Bluesky/stock widgets, on-device translation, sign-in, profile, settings and admin pages, the racer game.
install.limits.3: Saved data can be out of date. When the registry is refreshed, saved results are re-fetched the next time you open them online.
install.limits.4: The service worker only works over HTTPS (or localhost) and only in the production build.
install.limits.5: iPhone/iPad: no install prompt; Safari may wipe storage of a site you have not opened for about 7 days - installing to the Home Screen avoids that.
install.limits.6: Storage is limited by the browser quota (usually a share of free disk space). It can be cleared by the browser when space runs low.
install.cache.1: Clearing “site data” or “cookies and site data” in browser settings also deletes your history, favorites and settings stored on this device. They are not synced anywhere.
install.cache.2: Private/Incognito windows do not keep anything between sessions.
install.cache.3: If the app looks stale or broken after an update: close every app window, reopen it, or hard-reload (Ctrl+Shift+R).
install.cache.4: “Clear cached images” in the side menu only removes photos, logos and backgrounds; saved results are removed one by one in History or Favorites.
install.cache.5: On a shared device remember that saved searches stay on it until you remove them.
install.update.1: The app checks for a new version whenever it is opened or reloaded.
install.update.2: When one is ready a bar appears: press “Update” to reload into the new version, or “Later” to keep working.
install.update.3: “Later” is safe: the new version activates once every app window is closed and the app is opened again.
install.update.4: Nothing to do for the website in a browser tab - just reload the page.
install.remove.1: Android: long-press the icon → App info → Uninstall (or remove it from Chrome’s menu).
install.remove.2: Desktop Chrome/Edge: open the app → menu ⋮ in its title bar → “Uninstall Cars UA”.
install.remove.3: iPhone/iPad: long-press the icon → Remove App → Delete.
install.remove.4: Uninstalling may keep saved data. To wipe it too, clear the site data for carsua.app in browser settings (this deletes history and favorites).
install.best.1: Serve everything over HTTPS; keep the manifest complete: name, short_name, start_url, scope, display, theme/background colour, 192 and 512 px icons plus a maskable icon.
install.best.2: Precache the app shell; use runtime caching with the right strategy per resource - CacheFirst for immutable assets and images, NetworkFirst for pages, StaleWhileRevalidate for API data.
install.best.3: Cap every runtime cache (entry count and age) and version/clean old caches on update.
install.best.4: Serve sw.js, index.html and the manifest with Cache-Control: no-cache; give hashed assets a long immutable cache.
install.best.5: Let the user control updates (a prompt instead of silent skipWaiting) so code is never swapped mid-task.
install.best.6: Never cache authenticated or personal API responses, and never POST requests.
install.best.7: Offer a graceful offline state and fallback page; tell the user what works offline.
install.best.8: Show your own install button via beforeinstallprompt where supported, and explain Add to Home Screen on iOS.
install.best.9: Request persistent storage, test with Lighthouse and the DevTools Application panel, and add only the extras you really need (push, sync) - each adds permissions and upkeep.

co2.title: Emissions
co2.infoScore: 0 = clean, 100 = worst - a scale, not a percentage. Scored linearly from tailpipe CO₂ (g/km): 0 g/km = 0, 300 g/km or more = 100 (so 150 g/km = 50). A pure EV scores 0 because only the tailpipe is counted.
co2.infoCycle: Figures come from the {{cycle}} test cycle; different cycles are not directly comparable (EPA reads lower than WLTP).
co2.infoWltp: WLTP (Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicles Test Procedure) is the lab test used for new cars in the EU since 2017–2019. A car is driven on a rolling road through a standard cycle of about 30 minutes - city, suburban, rural and motorway phases up to 131 km/h - which is more realistic than the older NEDC (about 20 minutes, max 120 km/h). EPA is the US procedure; NEDC is the old European one.
co2.infoSources: Data: EEA (European Environment Agency) - official CO₂ monitoring of new cars registered in the EU, from manufacturers' WLTP/NEDC type approvals; EPA (US Environmental Protection Agency) - fuel economy and CO₂ of US-market vehicles, published at fueleconomy.gov.
co2.infoEstimate: An estimate for similar vehicles (same make, model and nearby year) - not a measurement of this exact car. Tap “similar vehicles” to browse them.

value.ua.expand: Show the EU value and the customs breakdown
value.sectionInfo:
Rough estimate of what it would cost to bring this car to Ukraine today. It is built in two steps: (1) the EU value - the Dutch new list price of this model and year (RDW open data) times a depreciation curve for its age; (2) Ukrainian customs on top - import duty, excise and VAT, calculated from the engine and age.
This is not a market price: it leaves out delivery, dealer margin and other fees, and mileage, condition and trim can move a real price far outside the range. Use it as a sanity check, then compare with real listings.
Switch the currency to euros, dollars or hryvnias (NBU rate of the day). The charts and the full explanation are in the “Charts and explanation” folder.
Source: RDW open data (CC0), the Dutch BPM depreciation schedule, Ukrainian customs law.

value.ua.nbuInfo: NBU stands for the National Bank of Ukraine, the country's central bank. Its official hryvnia rate for the day is what customs uses, so the euro and dollar amounts here are converted at that rate.

mot.help.test.title: MOT test
mot.help.test.body: The yearly roadworthiness inspection of a UK vehicle. Only normal tests are counted; re-tests after a failure are left out so a car is not counted twice.
mot.help.fail.title: Failed
mot.help.fail.body: The test ended in a fail: at least one item was bad enough that the car may not be used until it is repaired. The charts show the share of tests that failed.
mot.help.watch.title: Watch for (advisory)
mot.help.watch.body: An item that passed but that the tester noted as worn or deteriorating ("watch for it"). Still legal, but the early stage of what may fail next time. The share counts tests with at least one such note.
mot.help.dangerous.title: Dangerous
mot.help.dangerous.body: A fault DVSA classes as a direct and immediate risk to road safety: the car must not be driven until it is fixed. Shown as the share of tests that had one.
mot.help.prs.title: Pass after rectification
mot.help.prs.body: A fault found and fixed at the test station during the test. It counts as a pass, not as a failed test.
mot.help.share.title: Share of tests
mot.help.share.body: Tests with the problem divided by all tests in the same mileage band. It is a share of inspections, not a probability for this car.
mot.help.issueTests.title: Tests with the issue, not defects
mot.help.issueTests.body: A test is counted once per problem even if it has it several times (four worn tyres = one test with a tyre fault). So the numbers are shares of cars, not counts of defects.
mot.help.band.title: Mileage band
mot.help.band.body: Odometer reading at the test, converted from miles to km and grouped (0–25, 25–50 … thousand km). Find your own mileage and read that column.
mot.help.average.title: UK average
mot.help.average.body: The same figure for all models of this kind together (cars, vans or motorcycles) in the same mileage band: a quick way to see whether the model is better or worse than usual.
mot.help.sample.title: Sample size
mot.help.sample.body: How many tests the figures rest on. A band with fewer than 200 tests is not drawn. The numbers describe the model in the UK (right-hand drive, salted winter roads).
